note: Weekend sweep, Saturday 12 Sep 2026 SGT. Covers Friday 11 Sep's full US session (the CPI outcome, the equity/VIX reversal, and the metals whipsaw) plus a check for anything new since Friday's close. Crypto (24/7) showed continued Fed-repricing chop into the weekend but no distinct new weekend-only catalyst; no confirmed Hormuz ceasefire or escalation update dated after Thu 10 Sep was found, and Friday's Singapore STI close was not available in searchable sources (most recent confirmed STI print is Wed 9 Sep), so the SGX item below uses the freshest confirmed S-REIT-sector data instead of a single-day index close. Ranked by decision-relevance to the book, most important first.

items.headline: August CPI matches headline consensus but core runs hot; Sep 16 Fed hike odds jump to ~87-90%
items.summary: US CPI rose 0.4% m/m in August (3.4% y/y, in line with the 3.4% consensus), but core CPI rose 0.3% m/m -- a tenth above forecast -- keeping core at an elevated annual pace. CME FedWatch-tracked odds of a 25bp hike at the Sep 15-16 FOMC surged to roughly 87-90%, up from ~72% the day before and ~50-59% a week earlier, meaning a hike (not a cut or hold) is now the market's base case for a war-driven inflation shock.
items.actionable: A confirmed Fed hike into a war-inflation shock (rather than the cut the market spent most of 2026 pricing) is a genuine headwind for the levered silver/miners sleeve and SGX bank/REIT valuations via higher real yields -- size positions assuming Wednesday delivers the hike, not a surprise hold.

items.headline: FOMC meets Sep 15-16; a 25bp hike to 3.75-4.00% is now the base case, not a cut
items.summary: The Fed's next decision lands Wednesday 2pm ET with updated dot plots, off a current target range of 3.5%-3.75% set after a divided 9-3 vote to hold in July (three dissents favored hiking then). Markets now assign roughly 87-90% probability to a quarter-point hike given persistent war-driven energy inflation -- a sharp reversal from the rate-cut path priced for most of 2026.
items.actionable: This is the single biggest scheduled catalyst for the whole book next week -- the real surprise risk is a hold (not a hike), which would likely spark an outsized relief rally in miners and S-REITs alike given how heavily a hike is already priced.

items.headline: Gold and silver whipsaw through the CPI print, close near $4,385-4,389 and ~$65 despite 90% hike odds
items.summary: Gold opened Friday at its lowest level in over a month ahead of CPI, then reversed to trade near $4,385-4,389/oz (roughly +1.7% on the day) once the headline matched consensus; silver swung between a 2.6% intraday loss (to ~$64.90) and a recovery toward $65, with USAGOLD noting physical gold held above $4,385 even as the CPI print lifted rate-hike odds to 90%. The reversal suggests inflation-hedge/haven demand is, for now, outweighing the rate-hike headwind on an intraday basis.
items.actionable: Metals shrugging off a near-90%-priced hike is a constructive tell, but the scale of the intraday whipsaw (silver -2.6% before recovering) means Monday's open can gap either way -- avoid adding leverage to the miners sleeve until Wednesday's FOMC outcome is confirmed.

items.headline: S&P snaps four-day losing streak (+0.86% to 7,657) as VIX collapses ~11-12% to ~15.6-15.8
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose to roughly 7,657 (+0.86-0.9%), ending four straight down sessions, while the VIX fell about 11-12% to near 15.6-15.8 as Brent's ~2.7-3% pullback (to ~$104.68) and easing Treasury yields outweighed the hotter-than-expected core CPI. Tech led the rebound (Dell +10%, HPE +9%); the move reflects relief that inflation wasn't worse, not resolution of the hike outlook.
items.actionable: The vol collapse is a genuine short-term relief signal for risk assets, but it coexists with a near-90%-priced hike -- an unusual pairing that argues for using this calm to review hedges on the large cash pile rather than chasing the rally into next week's FOMC.

items.headline: Largest wave yet of US-Iran tanker strikes near the Strait of Hormuz; oil pushed above $108-109 before Friday's pullback
items.summary: Iran said it struck 10 vessels near the Strait of Hormuz -- described by Reuters as the largest declared wave of tit-for-tat shipping attacks since the war began in February 2026 -- with UKMTO reporting several merchant ships in the northern Gulf and Gulf of Oman hit by disabling fire overnight. The US separately struck three Iranian oil tankers in retaliation; no ceasefire or de-escalation has surfaced as of Saturday, and Brent had spiked above $108-109 (highest since May) before Friday's broader-market-driven pullback to ~$104.68.
items.actionable: This remains a worsening, not fading, conflict with no ceasefire in sight -- keep the oil/energy exposure and cash pile in place as hedges, and treat Friday's oil pullback as profit-taking/relief rather than a signal the Hormuz risk has passed.

items.headline: China's rare-earth export halt to the US and Japan deepens ahead of the Sep 24 Trump-Xi summit
items.summary: Chinese suppliers have refused to ship rare earths to US companies since early August, a squeeze that intensified after Beijing sanctioned the Responsible Business Alliance; yttrium exports to the US now run at roughly half of 2024 levels, while Japan recorded zero terbium exports and a 98% drop in yttrium shipments (Jan-Aug) versus a year earlier, alongside a 65% drop in gallium. China still controls roughly 99% of global heavy rare-earth processing, so near-term diversification isn't realistic before the summit.
items.actionable: The deepening squeeze is direct pre-summit leverage from Beijing and supports the ex-China rare-earth watchlist thesis into 24 Sep -- but remember the basket already sold off ~4-6% on Sep 10 purely on thaw-hope headlines, so a friendly summit outcome (not just an actual export resumption) could reverse gains sharply.

items.headline: MP Materials short interest at 20.4% of float as rare-earth curbs rally the stock; squeeze risk building into the summit
items.summary: MP Materials shares rallied (up roughly 10.5% year-to-date as of early September) after China's rare-earth export curbs on the US, with 18 analysts averaging a Strong Buy rating and a 12-month price target of $75.38 (about +47% from early-September levels); short interest sits at 20.4% of MP's available float. Lynas Rare Earths is also rebounding on US-government-backed supply-chain deals, though the two firms' prior partnership talks are reportedly not currently active.
items.actionable: High short interest in MP means any friendly summit headline (or an actual export resumption) could trigger an outsized squeeze -- worth sizing the watchlist entry with that asymmetry in mind rather than waiting for full confirmation.

items.headline: Hang Seng falls 1.3% to ~24,954 as Hormuz-driven oil spike revives inflation and tighter-policy fears
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index dropped 1.3% (about 320 points) to close near 24,954 as Brent's climb above $109/barrel on Hormuz shipping disruptions revived fears of higher inflation and tighter global monetary policy; property and China policy signals remain the dominant swing factor for HK equities heading into the Sep 24 Trump-Xi summit.
items.actionable: Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi are currently trading as macro/oil proxies rather than on company fundamentals -- expect continued correlation to Hormuz headlines and the summit outcome over the next two weeks rather than idiosyncratic moves.

items.headline: Silver on track for a sixth straight annual supply deficit; 2026 gap projected near 67 million ounces
items.summary: The silver market is heading for its sixth consecutive year where industrial and investment demand outstrips mine-plus-recycled supply, with the 2026 shortfall projected around 67 million ounces against total supply near 1.05 billion ounces. Mine output actually fell about 2% in 2026 despite record-high prices because roughly 70% of mined silver is a byproduct of lead/zinc/copper operations, and above-ground stockpiles have been drawn down by 762 million ounces since 2021.
items.actionable: The structural deficit underpins the long-term case for the silver-miners sleeve independent of this week's Fed-driven volatility -- a reason to hold through the CPI/FOMC noise rather than trade around it, though it doesn't offset near-term rate-hike-driven downside risk.

items.headline: Singapore's REIT sector down 8.2% YTD versus the STI's +24.6% as the market re-prices Fed hikes
items.summary: The FTSE ST All-Share REIT Index is down 8.2% year-to-date as of early September, badly lagging the Straits Times Index's 24.6% gain, as investors shift from pricing Fed rate cuts to pricing hikes. Analysts still hold an overweight-but-selective stance on S-REITs, favoring names with fixed-rate debt and defensive earnings, with sector yield spreads over Singapore's 10-year bond still wide (~3.7 percentage points).
items.actionable: With a Fed hike now ~87-90% priced for Wednesday, expect continued pressure on Keppel REIT/Mapletree PACT-type names until the FOMC outcome is confirmed -- stay selective/defensive in the REIT sleeve rather than adding on dips this week.

items.headline: Bitcoin and Ethereum choppy into the weekend on Fed rate-hike repricing, no distinct new weekend catalyst
items.summary: Bitcoin's Friday session ranged from an open near $76,530 to an intraday high of $79,837 before settling back near $77,000-77,400, while Ethereum traded near $2,450-2,470, as the same rate-hike repricing that moved stocks (odds jumping from ~69% to ~87-90% intraday) whipsawed crypto alongside equities. As of Saturday morning SGT, no distinct new weekend-specific catalyst (regulatory, exchange, or macro) has surfaced beyond continued digestion of Friday's CPI/Fed repricing.
items.actionable: Crypto is trading as a high-beta rates proxy right now rather than an independent driver -- treat it as a read-through risk-appetite indicator for the book rather than a standalone position; a confirmed Wednesday hike would likely pressure BTC/ETH further.

items.headline: Brent tumbles ~2.7-3% to ~$104.68 on CPI-day relief, but remains up double digits over the past month on the Hormuz war
items.summary: Brent crude fell roughly 2.7-3% Friday to about $104.68/barrel, retreating from Thursday's spike above $108-109 (a four-month high) as fears of a much worse CPI print proved overdone. Oil is still up roughly 9% over five days and about 19% over the past month, entirely a function of the ongoing US-Iran Strait of Hormuz tanker war rather than any change in physical fundamentals.
items.actionable: Friday's pullback is a relief valve, not a resolution -- Hormuz remains the primary tail risk underpinning the energy position, so treat any single-day drop as noise rather than a reason to trim the Iran-war hedge.
